I did not enjoy Below Zero to the same degree as the original Subnautica, which sucks because there are many new mechanics in this game that I really like or at least think are neat ([spoiler] Cold System, Quantum Chest, Recycler, Vehicle Teleportation, Monke tithe collection [/spoiler]), but, ironically, lack depth. The underwater world feels smaller with not much reason to go to more than 2-3 biomes for materials or base building, new mechanics are situational/heavily localized, and just another way to get resources if picking them off the ground felt too same-y for your gameplay. There's no real way of conveniently moving a lot of resources easily. There are ways of attempting to do so with new mechanics, but they are, at best, only doable in the late-end game, tedious, and the hard cap is still nothing compared to having a Cyclops.

Just below 2 hours in. 
I want to like it, I really do. Subnautica was a terrific game, which had me hooked from the first second. Below Zero failed to do that. Will it get better later on? Maybe. But I cannot ask myself to go there on the mere hope that MAYBE it gets better. 

Pros: 
The Environment is beautiful. 
The dynamic weather is a sight to behold, one of the things missing in the first part. 

Cons: 
Getting the Seaglide did not feel like an achievement, since I got it essentially instantly. 
The loss of a silent protagonist ruined immersion for me.
The over-the-top sound effects when Robin consumes something are annoying.
The PDA's much more expressive, quippy delivery didn't work for me. I strongly preferred the original's calm, clinical AI voice.
Resources came too easily, reducing the survival feeling.
The game felt more guided, almost as if they were holding my hand. 
Subnautica had rather few "humerous" voicelines, which made them hit hard and good, BZ is overloaded with bad jokes. 
I found little reason to explore, since withing 30 minutes I had my initial storage filled to the brim with everything I needed. 

Overall, I liked some aspects. But they killed the immersion, something I want from a survival game. SBZ unfortunatly not only falls short of Subnatica, but straight up didn't jump.
Snow and pretty sky. I got freaked out when the playable character talked

Right out the gate the vibe is wrong, the playable character is quipping, and the story is very personal and we are in a story driven situation, it just made the game feel less interesting to me, in subnautica you were stranded and alone slowly unraveling the situation on the planet, and even the over arching alien involvement was left vague and mysterious. In BZ everything is narrative and up front making it feel more like chores than survival. 

The landscapes were interesting but the new vehicles were less interesting to me, no cyclops sucks, and adding more types of rocks to break early game was really boring and made me not want to play. If you played Subnautica its better in almost every way so there is no reason to play this.

Subnautica Below Zero is a disappointment, it unfortunately scales down the best part of the first game and puts spotlight on the bad parts. The exploration this time around is much more limited, the map is both smaller and also emptier than the first game and while the game has some cool biomes like the Twisty Bridges and Lilypad Islands it unfortunately cannot save the experience. Not to mention the game for a bizarre reason has a much more prominent onland part, why? Seriously it is as if the dev team decided to bring forward the worst parts of the first game and make them even more annoying.

Same goes for the story, which tries to tackle 2 plot threads, you start out going to the planet to figure out what happened to your sister and to my surprise this plot gets sidelined so hard to the point it seems the game itself forgets about it because you can finish the game without even figuring it out. It is as if that thread became a sidequest except its the reason why you came to the planet in the first place. 

Now there are some upsides, the building part of the game has been improved with more things to build (these were however patched to the first game so it is no longer that much of an improvement), the graphics stay strong as does the sound design and the few cool biomes are actually really cool. The performance and pop in have also improved but the game slows you down to make the small world seem a little bigger which might be the only reason why.

Achievement wise just like the first game you basically only need to complete the story, do a bunch of crafting which you will likely do naturally as you pla…

Same price as subnautica 1? quarter of the content and less than half the map size from the first? terrible retconned story with an annoyingly voiced protag? Literal copy/pasted content from the first except in exchange for the speedy seamouth and sub we get some frankenstein mangled modular truck? Terribly forced land content? Genuinely what is this game? 

This game should have remained a DLC like it was supposed to be initially but the devs are greedy.

Subnautica: Below Zero is a good game, but it never reached the magic of the first one for me.

The biggest improvement is that the world doesn't feel completely lonely anymore. Having Marguerit around was awesome, and I actually enjoyed seeing another living person instead of just listening to PDA logs. AL-AN was also a fun companion throughout the story.

The Seatruck is another highlight. I liked being able to detach modules and even leave them around the map as makeshift markers.

That said, I felt like Below Zero lost what made the original so special. The map is much smaller and filled with narrow caves, tiny openings, and endless icebergs. Exploration often felt more frustrating than exciting. In the first game, discovering massive wrecks was one of my favorite parts. Below Zero doesn't have that same sense of scale or wonder.

It also felt much grindier. I found myself wanting to finish the game rather than taking my time exploring. The story was decent, but I was disappointed that we still don't really learn what ultimately happened to the Architects.

Overall:

🌊 Subnautica (2018): 9/10
🧊 Below Zero: 6/10

If you loved the first game, Below Zero is still worth playing. Just don't expect it to capture the same feeling of mystery, exploration, and scale that made the original unforgettable.

I absolutely loved the first Subnautica. It was immersive, terrifying, mysterious, and easily one of the best survival games I have ever played. Unfortunately, this sequel feels like a heavily watered-down version of it.

The gameplay itself is still decent, but everything feels more childish, family-friendly, easier, less scary, and ultimately much more boring. The map feels smaller, nighttime is nowhere near as dark or oppressive, and the creatures are much less intimidating. Even the Leviathans feel weak compared to the first game.

There is also very little genuinely new technology, and the removal of the Cyclops was a huge downgrade. Its replacement, the Sea Truck, is an absolute abomination. It is slow, clumsy, awkward to control, and terrible in narrow areas. I genuinely hated using it.

The story is also mediocre, the protagonist is forgettable, and the main objective involving her sister somehow feels optional and disconnected from the rest of the game.

I genuinely tried to give this game a fair chance because of how much I loved the first one, but I simply could not finish it. It is not completely terrible, but compared to Subnautica 1, it feels safer, smaller, less ambitious, and far less memorable.

Overall, just mid. A very disappointing sequel.

While Below Zero is still technically "Subnautica," it is absolutely NOT worth being sold as an entire standalone title. They really should’ve stuck with the original plan to make it a DLC expansion for a much lower price point. The map is a massive downgrade compared to the first game; the world is way smaller, shallower, and completely crammed. In the original, you had this incredible sense of vast, terrifying, open ocean isolation. Here, everything feels claustrophobic, and half the time you're forced out of the water completely to navigate the incredibly clunky, frustrating land biomes on a Snowfox that handles like a shopping cart with a broken wheel.

The story is also complete a**. The biggest issue is how disjointed and unorganized the whole narrative feels. They completely scrapped the superior plot they had during the early stages of Early Access. For anyone who doesn't know, there was a totally different, much more coherent story written by the original writer where your sister Sam was alive up on a space station communicating with you, you started in a fully staffed research base before a meteor strike hit, and the dynamic with AL-AN was way more interesting and less cooperative right off the bat. You can actually still play those early 2019/2020 builds (like EA8) today if you do some easy trickery with the Steam console using download_depot commands to downgrade your game version, or you can just watch the old gameplay archives on YouTube. The negative reception stems mainly from Early Access and modern Subnautica: Below Zero is an incredibly fun journey. The leviathans in this game are not as PTSD-inducing as its older counterpart in my opinion, which makes it a good game for those too queasy to play the first. The story does not require a playthrough of the first to understand, though there are some references to the original Subnautica since this takes place on the same planet, 4546B.

After 40 hours of playtime in Subnautica 2, completing its current state, I decided to try this game since it was the most forgettable experience, and poorly received amongst certain people for its diversion to a more story-focused game rather than a survive and escape the planet kind of game. The game features classic survival, hardcore and creative modes, but also 'freedom' mode, where you are in the survival state but do not have to manage water and food consumption, making the game very friendly to those who do not want to micromanage themselves. Focus on the exploring if you really want to!

Rating: ★★★★☆ (4/5)
Subnautica: Below Zero is undeniably a great game, but to be completely honest, it doesn't quite reach the legendary status of the original.
Visually, the game is a massive step up. The graphics are stunning, the icy environments are breathtaking, and the upgraded creatures and biomes look incredible. The refined building mechanics and quality-of-life improvements make crafting and base-building feel smoother than ever.
However, something about the overall vibe and feeling just doesn't hit the same way the first game did. The original Subnautica nailed a rare, terrifying sense of isolation and vast, open-ocean mystery. Below Zero feels a bit more compact and voice-driven, which trades away some of that eerie, lonely atmosphere that made the first one so unforgettable.
Maybe it’s just my deep love and nostalgia for the original, but Planet 4546B felt a little more magical the first time around.

Subnautica Below Zero is a disappointment, it unfortunately scales down the best part of the first game and puts spotlight on the bad parts. Not to mention the game for a bizarre reason has a much more prominent onland part, why? Seriously it is as if the dev team decided to bring forward the worst parts of the first game and make them even more annoying.

Same goes for the story, which tries to tackle 2 plot threads, you start out going to the planet to figure out what happened to your sister and to my surprise this plot gets sidelined so hard to the point it seems the game itself forgets about it because you can finish the game without even figuring it out. It is as if that thread became a sidequest except its the reason why you came to the planet in the first place. 

Now there are some upsides, the building part of the game has been improved with more things to build (these were however patched to the first game so it is no longer that much of an improvement), the graphics stay strong as does the sound design and the few cool biomes are actually really cool. The performance and pop in have also improved but the game slows you down to make the small world seem a little bigger which might be the only reason why.

Achievement wise just like the first game you basically only need to complete the story, do a bunch of crafting which you will likely do naturally as you pla…
Too much time spent on land

Honestly, I would not recommend this game. Incomparable to the first one. Unlike the first one, you start the game on a rescue mission in search of your lost sister instead of accidentally crash landing. They decide to add your character to have dialog. I thought it was gonna be a cool change from the first one to actually have a different feel to the story. Your character ends up becoming more or less annoying. Talking about herself and her feelings constantly. To finally find someone else in the game,  just to find out that they're just as annoying and unhelpful as your own character. When you find out what happened to your sister, your person doesn't care and moves on with the rest of the poorly written story. 

Besides the poorly written storyline there is a creative world full of nothing. The world's full of new biomes and creatures that seem interesting, but, there's nothing there, it's empty. Although the map was small, I felt like I kept running in circles and getting lost. It seemed so much harder to navigate than the first 1. It's extremely hard to find things to scan to research. And once you find items to create and craft, there's almost no point to do any of it. The world's half the size of the original game, and yet it feels like it takes twice as long to get anywhere. They got rid of the cyclone and added the sea truck, which absolutely sucks. 

So they added a bit more land exploration, which seemed pretty cool, but the thing is, you can't survive more than 30 seconds on land. And they made our woman character not able to jump over anything. I'm talking about small rocks. No, you're not jumping over nothing.  You can make a snowsuit, but by the time you figure that out, you can already make a prawn suit and just finish the whole land spot. 

The gameplay was OK. I was just upset with how short the game was and how empty I felt after beating it. It felt purposeless to collect and build up a base or do anything cool with any of the new stuff they added…

Overall, a very big downgrade from the original.

Sound design feels a lot louder compared to the first game, which makes it lose the feel the first game had. The Ice Worm and Snowfox are buggy beyond belief, that entire section of the game was a slog to get through. Story is kinda meh, its alright but some parts, particularly in Sam's storyline are incredibly underwhelming. 

Some parts I liked:

The art direction of the game is phenomenal, all the areas look really nice and are aesthetically pleasing. I like the seatruck as a vehicle, I do prefer the vehicles from Sub 1, but the seatruck works better for this game. Music is brilliant. The story with AL-AN is really fascinating and cool. Base building is better than the original. 

Not a bad game imo, its defo got reasons to play it. However the downsides are just a bit too big for me to ignore.

While Below Zero is still technically "Subnautica," it is absolutely NOT worth being sold as an entire standalone title. They really should’ve stuck with the original plan to make it a DLC expansion for a much lower price point. The map is a massive downgrade compared to the first game; the world is way smaller, shallower, and completely crammed. In the original, you had this incredible sense of vast, terrifying, open ocean isolation. Here, everything feels claustrophobic, and half the time you're forced out of the water completely to navigate the incredibly clunky, frustrating land biomes on a Snowfox that handles like a shopping cart with a broken wheel.

The story is also complete a**. The biggest issue is how disjointed and unorganized the whole narrative feels. They completely scrapped the superior plot they had during the early stages of Early Access. For anyone who doesn't know, there was a totally different, much more coherent story written by the original writer where your sister Sam was alive up on a space station communicating with you, you started in a fully staffed research base before a meteor strike hit, and the dynamic with AL-AN was way more interesting and less cooperative right off the bat. You can actually still play those early 2019/2020 builds (like EA8) today if you do some easy trickery with the Steam console using download_depot commands to downgrade your game version, or you can just watch the old gameplay archives on YouTube. It's wild to see how much the devs panicked, changed writers, and completely rewrote everything midway through development while awkwardly trying to reuse the exact same map assets and voice logs.

Because they essentially jerry-rigged a completely new story over an old map layout, the pacing is totally broken. It's incredibly easy to accidentally mess up your story progression sequence. You can stumble into later plot points out of order, making the narrative feel entirely half-assed. Your main driving motivation…

Subnautica: Below Zero takes a slightly different approach compared to the original game by focusing more on narrative and atmosphere while still maintaining the survival mechanics that make the series so engaging. The frozen environment feels hostile in a completely different way, with snowstorms, icy caves, and freezing temperatures adding constant pressure during exploration. This creates a more grounded and claustrophobic experience, especially when moving between underwater depths and dangerous land sections.

What makes the game stand out is how it mixes calm exploration with moments of uncertainty and tension. Discovering abandoned facilities, strange lifeforms, and hidden parts of the map always feels rewarding, especially because the game rarely interrupts the player with unnecessary guidance. The addition of new tools, creatures, and vehicles keeps progression satisfying throughout the adventure, while the smaller but denser world design makes every biome feel distinct and memorable.

I played this right after I finished Subnautica. Most things as far as gameplay, building your seabase, using the fabricator, and the UI feel very familiar, but the environment is very different and there's a new mechanic of temperature which you have to manage when out of the water. In practice, this just feels like managing your oxygen when under the water.

This game is smaller than Subnautica, which means there's less to explore, and also means you're given less space to navigate around leviathans. This makes certain areas frustrating to navigate through, particularly in the late game.

The new seatruck is a welcome addition though, and I hope to see it in future games. It's nice to be able to bring a whole base with you, set up camp, and then navigate tighter or more dangerous areas with just a few modules of your mobile base, versus the cyclops where the whole thing has to come with you.

The other thing that I feel is a downgrade from the previous game is the story, or more specifically, the way the game leads you toward story events and locations. In the previous game you would get radio messages every so often that would give you a direction to go, but in this game you either find the story beats or you don't. And since part of the story is optional and easy to miss, this likely means many people finish the game while missing major elements of the story.

Overall, if you liked Subnautica, you will like this game. Which one you like more probably depends on personal preferences, but for me, the original is the better of the two. Still a good game though!

Subnautica Below Zero is a good, but flawed game. It is worth playing through if you loved the first game, but you need to dial down your expectations before playing it. This game was supposted to be a DLC but scope creeped itself into a full fledged game. It also underwent a writer change midway through development which you notice early on.

Here are the main critisms:
-the map is way smaller than the original game, its not as open and features many caves and land sections, which makes gameplay frustrating and boring at times, you can easily get lost since some locations are literally a labyrinth
-the creatures and environment are forgiving and are even less threatening than in SN1 (i died only once due to a collision bug...)
-the story, characters and writing is not good and nonsensical at times
-vehicles from the previous game have been removed and replaced with a slower, more boring sea truck (prawn suit is still there)
-gathering materials, finding blueprints and progressing the story isnt as straight forward as in SN1 (i got confused at times, missed blueprints and had to use an online map and google on what to do next, i didnt have to do that as much in the original game)
-PDA voice is very annoying for no reason
-PDA logs are very barebones at times

Heres whats better/just as good:
-the biomes are beautiful (maybe even prettier than SN1, land sections look acceptable now, not like a PS2 game)
-base building is similar, but you have more rooms and items for decoration
-wrecks and important locations feature more variety in design
-its more subnautica if you liked the first game

Id recommend picking it up when its on sale for a fraction of the original price.

Went into the game hearing all of the criticism and after completing everything the game has to offer, it's honestly overrated and not that bad of a game. It's pretty much more Subnautica but that isn't to say it doesn't have its flaws. This spin off installment is a bit more narrative focused than the first Subnautica that is admittedly confusing to follow and there are some parts of the game that could've been more fleshed out such as the land exploration segments. The map is also smaller compared to the original but this is due to it being conceptualized as DLC before the ideas became too big for it just to be DLC, but there is still quite a bit to do. Despite this though there were lots of aspects I really like about the game like the seatruck, having to evade certain creatures/ leviathans, the very nice looking biomes, the nice additions to base building and the overall progression of the game. If you liked Subnautica, I think you'll like this game as well.

Wonderful continuation of the first story.   Fills in some much needed lore and really rounds out the whole tale of Alterra vs. The Planet,

BZ feels shorter than the first game.    It kind of has to be, because the beginning of the first game is pure grind, searching the map for the stuff you need to build up your capabilities.   Since they clearly used the same engine, same materials and same recipes as the first game, it would have been unacceptable repetition to force people to re-live the early game of Subnautica.   So, with BZ, you get to the mid-game much faster, able to build a sizeable base and strike out exploring with less hassle.

The map feels a bit smaller than Subnautica, but is has the same basic layout, with safe shallows, and a variety of interesting deeper areas that get progressively more dangerous.

The addition of the SeaTruck was lovely, but if I have one complaint is that's the devs still kind of miss what we really want to do.   There's not enough stuff to fill a big base, so every base just ends up with three or four small modules, and then nothing much else.    The Seatruck can be made longer, but it becomes slower and unwieldy.... Which would be fine if (like the cyclops) you could trick it out inside with posters, cabinets, tables, shelves, etc, so it becomes a mobile base.  But sadly it never quite becomes a proper mobile base, unless you add three or four storage units..  Sonar pod would have been nice.. Or a mini nuclear reactor pod, or an observation pod (all glass)...  

All of this is just wishful thinking anyway.... The game plays really well.     Finding artefacts is challenging and a little time consuming.  One snowy area is very  labyrinthine, and I totally got lost trying to find things.   It's fun though, that you stumble around for hours, but if you keep your eyes peeled and do a little exploring, you can find a quick route to almost everywhere, including back out into the sea.


Definitely play this if you liked …

The environment and biomes are incredibly shallow, unoriginal, and uninteresting. Sure, the first game had the islands, but those had good reasons to be there, this game has no reason to be like this.

Story in this game is also the most cliche, uninspired  POS, giving you no reason to actually want to explore the world, i had no desire or idea why the ♥♥♥♥ should i care about any of this, unlike with the first game. As for the characters, there is no good character to speak of. olid game. I really enjoyed the first Subnautica, so I wanted to try this one as well. Compared to the first game, this one has a smaller map but more abandoned bases, many of them located above the surface. The graphics are good, and the story is decently executed, although it feels slightly unfinished.

This time, the developers tried to tell a more linear story than in the first game, which may or may not be a good thing depending on the player. The story also seems to be split into two separate plotlines, and I think one of them is not fully developed and is overshadowed by the other. It almost feels like the developers wanted to tell one story but added another one later just to give the main character a reason to visit the planet. That idea is fine, but I think it needed slightly better execution.

The main downside of this game, in my opinion, is that the vehicles were heavily nerfed. For example, the Prawn Suit can no longer build momentum with the Grappling Arm and Jump Jet Upgrade, making it feel much slower and less enjoyable to use.

The first game felt much more mysterious and full of unanswered questions. As a player, you had to explore the world and discover clues on your own with very little guidance from the radio. olid game. I really enjoyed the first Subnautica, so I wanted to try this one as well. Although many new things were added (biomes, vehicles, voice acting) and a couple of tweaks were made (recipes, outcrops), many of them were neutral or lackluster (especially predators and leviathans), with little of them being positive e.g. expanding the world we got from its prequel

But my main issue is the chaotic progression of the story (which is better described as nonexistent) and two of the largest and most impactful areas in the game: [spoiler] Arctic Spires, which is a barren desert with just two points of interest,[/spoiler] and [spoiler]Crystal Caves, which are as empty as Spires except they are littered with Prawn Suit arm fragments (literally)[/spoiler]. The starting story (the investigation of the sister's death) seems like a poor excuse for the whole game to take place, as the real main story, which took me 15 hours to find, is about something else (I ignored one of the first beacon marks in the game and focused on exploration of other parts of the world).

The first Subnautica was the first survival/building/exploring game that clicked for me; the narrative, survival mechanics and gameplay loop really worked well together in a way that I'd not seen before. Through clever design, I felt like I had both freedom to explore and yet was never confused about what my goals were to advance the plot. 

I had hoped Below Zero would recapture that magic, and while a lot of the core gameplay is the same (and there was the initial magic of getting up and running, finding blueprints and which zones hold which resources), the game never really hangs together in the same way. The above surface cold zone is ok but feels oddly out-of-place, the narrative feels confused and my goals were often unclear, leaving me to putter around trying to work out what to do next to advance things. 

So - I enjoyed the first 17 or so hours of playtime and wonder what the negative reviewers were talking about (I even liked the modular Sea Truck!) but after that I've been roaming around try to work out what to do in a way that is frustrating more than enjoyable. The improvements it has over the original are really good, but they are not really improvements anymore considering they were retroactively added to the original game through an update. So the resulting game feels very underwhelming. I really wanted to write a detailed positive review of what I love about Below Zero, but a bug that halted my base building was the last straw. I shouldn't have to force myself to dig through crap to find the gold in the game, the game should be competent enough to show its strengths on its own. Unfortunately, in its current state, it is definitely not.

I think Below Zero is still worth experiencing, but go into it expecting to be punished for trying to engage with it more than surface-level. I was willing to overlook all the rough parts and Recommend the game with some critique, but when the issues started to get in the way of my gameplay I just lost all patience, I'm sorry. I cannot respect a game that doesn't respect its players. Might edit this review in the future to add my more detailed critique.
